summary: Find the person who trusts nobody and is trusted by everybody else (or -1).
mainInsight: In graph terms the judge has outdegree 0 and indegree n - 1. A single net-trust score (in - out) per person is enough: the judge is the only person with score n - 1.

approaches.name: Separate in/out degree counts
approaches.summary: Two maps or arrays; find out == 0 and in == n - 1.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal; a single net-trust array is more compact.

promptVariants: What degrees define the town judge in a directed graph?
Which quantity identifies the judge with one array?
options: Outdegree 0 and indegree n - 1; net score in - out = n - 1
Indegree 0 and outdegree n - 1; net score out - in = n - 1
The highest outdegree in the whole graph, always
Equal in-degree and out-degree for everyone else
cards.answer: Outdegree 0 and indegree n - 1; net score in - out = n - 1
cards.explanation: The judge trusts nobody and everyone else trusts the judge.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Indegree 0 and outdegree n - 1; net scor: That describes the opposite (a person who trusts everyone).

promptVariants: Why is the net-trust score n - 1 unique to the judge?
Why can't two people be judges?
cards.answer: Any non-judge who trusts at least one person has out >= 1, so in - out <= (n - 1) - 1 = n - 2 even if everyone else trusted them. Only a person with out = 0 and in = n - 1 reaches n - 1, and two such people would have to trust each other (a contradiction with out = 0).
keyPoints: Non-judges have out >= 1 or in < n - 1
cards.explanation: That is why one array of scores suffices.

promptVariants: Time complexity (n people, E trust pairs): ___
Complete the statement: Time complexity (n people, E trust pairs): ___
cards.explanation: One pass over the edges and one over the people.

promptVariants: What is the space and what is unusual about reading `incoming[i + 1]` on a defaultdict?
How could the arrays be simplified?
cards.answer: O(n) for the counts. Reading a missing key on a defaultdict inserts it (a small side effect); pre-sizing arrays of length n + 1 avoids this and is faster.

promptVariants: What is returned for n = 1 and trust = []?
Who is the judge when there is one person?
cards.explanation: outdegree 0 and indegree n - 1 = 0 hold for the only person. (1: the lone person trusts nobody and everyone else, i.e. nobody, trusts them)
